sentences.text: Wilaru was specialized for a more terrestrial lifestyle compared to other presbyornithids, as indicated by its tarsometatarsal morphology. It possessed spurs and knobs on its carpals, similar to modern waterfowl.
Wilaru prideauxi was larger and more robust than Wilaru tedfordi, suggesting a specialization toward a terrestrial lifestyle.
The genus name Wilaru means "stone curlew" in the Diyari language.
The spurs and knobs on Wilaru were likely used for fighting and territorial behavior, unlike the gregarious habits of earlier presbyornithids.
The type species Wilaru tedfordi was discovered in the Namba Formation of the Lake Eyre Basin in north-eastern South Australia.
The species name tedfordi honors Richard H. Tedford, who led the 1971 expedition that collected the fossil material.
The holotype of Wilaru tedfordi is a left humerus, and the holotype of Wilaru prideauxi is a right tarsometatarsus.
A 2025 study based on a nearly complete skull of Vegavis confirmed Wilaru as a member of the Presbyornithidae family within Anseriformes.
Wilaru lived in Australia during the Late Oligocene to Early Miocene, approximately 26 to 22 million years ago.
The fossil record of Wilaru spans from the Chattian to the Burdigalian stages, between 27.3 and 15.98 million years ago.
Wilaru coexisted with various anatid and anseranatid species with little ecological competition.
